contract_grounding.note: Violates-declaration self-check: the observed phenomenon (200+success on an ambiguous request, per the self-check's 'illegal value silently accepted' shape) is grounded as follows — the filter in the S2 body is individually WELL-FORMED, so the assertion's literal '400 on an invalid filter' trigger is not met word-for-word; the violated promise is the endpoint's documented request grammar (Request section: 'PointIdsList object Required OR FilterSelector object Required' — an exactly-one selector) together with the endpoint's documented 400='bad request / validation error' disposition face (raw_knowledge expected_responses): a body matching both branches is a validation error per the API's own oneOf grammar, yet it received the 200-success envelope and was executed. The disposition chosen: NOT 'value genuinely compliant' — the request violates the documented selector grammar, and the server's own S1 zero-branch 400 proves that grammar is enforced on the adjacent boundary, making the S2 acceptance an inconsistency in the server's own validation rather than undocumented territory. The 200-success promise is thereby consumed by a non-valid request. source_grounding.call_chain_traced: src/actix/api/update_api.rs:84 Json<PointsSelector> (serde deserializes the raw body) -> #[serde(untagged)] enum tries variants IN ORDER: PointIdsSelector(PointIdsList) matches {"points":[2]} and SILENTLY IGNORES the sibling "filter" key because PointIdsList carries no deny_unknown_fields (lib/shard/src/operations/point_ops.rs:41-48) -> Validate impl (lib/collection/src/operations/point_ops.rs:28-35) only validates the CHOSEN variant's inner content, so it cannot see the dropped key -> do_delete_points (src/common/update.rs:412-447) matches the already-resolved variant and executes DeletePoints{ids} -> update() applies it. No mutual-exclusion/ambiguity validation exists anywhere on this path; the only grammar enforcement is the zero-branch rejection (no variant matches -> serde error surfaced as 400 'data did not match any variant of untagged enum PointsSelector'). Mechanically predicts the observed resolution: points branch wins, filter dropped — exactly what the live repro showed (id 2 deleted, id 3 grp=red survived). Asymmetry note: the second branch's inner Filter DOES use deny_unknown_fields (lib/segment/src/types.rs:3793), so strictness exists in the same type family but is absent exactly on the first variant that wins ties.
source_grounding.verification_note: No validation enforcing the documented exactly-one (OR/oneOf) selector grammar on the REST path beyond the zero-branch rejection. NOT by_design_in_source: the enum and PointIdsList carry no intent comment (no 'intentionally'/'by design'/'we don't guarantee' marker anywhere on this path), and bare unannotated leniency is barred from the by_design reading; the codebase demonstrably applies deny_unknown_fields elsewhere in the same selector family (Filter, WithPayload, PayloadSelectorInclude/Exclude in lib/segment/src/types.rs, with a test_deny_unknown_fields at line 4390), so the absence on PointIdsList is an unannotated gap. The gRPC face is structurally immune (prost oneof permits at most one selector field), making this a REST-face-specific gap.
